findings.title: [F1] Unauthenticated raw, non-graceful, inconsistent errors via GET /redirect (TypeError) and POST /api/Feedbacks/ (raw Sequelize WHERE) — error handling challenge id=27
findings.analysis: Unauthenticated requests to two different routes produce raw, non-graceful, inconsistent server errors: (1) GET /redirect -> 500 with an Express error page titled 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading includes)'; (2) POST /api/Feedbacks/ with plain-text body 'plain text line' -> 500 with an Express error page titled 'Error: WHERE parameter "captchaId" has invalid "undefined" value' (raw Sequelize DB error exposing the internal parameter name and its undefined value). Verified byte-identical on fresh repeats of each request. The two routes expose different raw error styles (JavaScript TypeError vs SQL WHERE error) rather than a sanitized, consistent user-facing error policy. Mapping: errorHandlingChallenge id=27 — 'Provoke an error that is neither very gracefully nor consistently handled.' Mutation-fragility disclosed: POST invalid JSON to /api/Products/ returns 401 UnauthorizedError ('No Authorization header was found') on this boot, i.e. that trigger is auth-gated now, not raw-error; the retained claim rests on the two byte-stable triggers above. Benign control: ordinary routes (e.g. GET /) return clean 200 shell responses, so the 500 raw errors are application errors, not routing failures.
findings.false_positive_check: The 500 responses appear for arbitrary unauthenticated callers (no Authorization required) with raw error text, and the two triggers yield mutually different error types (TypeError vs WHERE error), proving inconsistent handling rather than a benign consistent error page. The raw text leaks internal values ('captchaId') and route-level control flow. The /api/Products/ invalid-JSON 401 is documented separately as a mutation-fragile gated trigger and is NOT part of this finding. Benign routes (GET /) return 200 cleanly, ruling out a routing-404/500 explanation for the raw errors.

secondary_trigger.note: independent reproduction yielding a different raw error type (raw Sequelize WHERE), confirming inconsistency

findings.title: [F2] Unauthenticated exposure of Prometheus observability telemetry including LLM usage gauges via GET /metrics — exposed metrics challenge id=97
findings.analysis: GET /metrics returns HTTP 200 text/plain without any Authorization header (~26000 B), serving Prometheus-format observability telemetry that is not present in the pinned v20.2.0 base image: http_requests_count by status, process_*, nodejs_version_info, juiceshop_version_info {version 20.2.0}, juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total 0 and juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total 0 (LLM token-usage counters exposed to any caller), juiceshop_orders_placed_total, juiceshop_users_registered_total, juiceshop_wallet_balance_total, juiceshop_cheat_score, and juiceshop_challenges_solved by difficulty/category. Mapping: exposedMetricsChallenge id=97. Verified on fresh repeats with identical presence of the llm_* gauges; a secrets scan of the response (password, token, key, secret, credential, api_key) finds no sensitive values — the exposure is operational telemetry, not credential leakage. The app-internal challenges_solved gauges read 0 across all categories on this boot (dynamic auto-solve state drift), but the unauthenticated telemetry itself is the finding and is stable.
findings.false_positive_check: No Authorization header is required (whoami -> {user: {}} unauthenticated); 200 on repeated fresh requests; the llm_* and juiceshop_* gauges are absent from the pinned v20.2.0 baseline, confirming this is a mutation-introduced surface. The response contains no password/token/key/secret/credential lines (scan-negative), so the finding is the unauthenticated telemetry exposure, not secret leakage. Not benign: the pinned baseline image does not serve /metrics, so the surface did not exist in the original application and is presented publicly.
